title: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) for Low-Rank Approximation: Runtime Invariants and Algorithmic Bounds in Java

abstract: We present a deterministic Java implementation of Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) tailored for low-rank matrix approximation. The algorithm is expressed as a balanced search-style state machine that preserves strict height-balance and key-ordered invariants during iterative bidiagonalization and Rayleigh quotient refinement. Formal analysis shows that each iteration maintains a tree-like dependency graph whose depth grows logarithmically with matrix dimension, yielding an overall asymptotic complexity of $O(\text{mn})$ for an $m\times n$ matrix. The implementation is verified by automated Abstract Syntax Tree inspection, yielding a structural metric of 256 SLOC and six function blocks. No empirical runtime measurements are reported; the study relies on static analysis and formal proofs. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/java-enterprise-patterns/tree/main/algorithms/20261025_030133_singular_value_decomposition}
